prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedarbell/Regional Flow Platform=Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System.Airports:Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport.Elements:Demand Prediction Service(Marlinstone);Weather Ingest Gateway(Orchard);Capacity Assessment Module;Slot Allocation Engine(Blueharbor:transition-training);Airport CDM Portal(Foxglove);Digital Briefing Room;Tower Sequence Manager;Ramp Movement Board;Departure Metering Service;Arrival Regulation Console;Contingency Operations Console;Flight Data Exchange;Surface Surveillance Adapter;Airline Interface Adapter;Alert Distribution Hub;Performance Analytics Warehouse;Audit Event Ledger;Identity Access Service;Business Rules Registry;Time Synchronization Service;Common Situation Display;Handling Resource Planner;Collaborative Decision Log.Indicators:North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter/East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor/Sector Load Monitor/Gate Conflict Detector.Actors:Regional Flow Manager(Copperfin);Airline Operations Coordinator(Saffron);Airline Operations Centre;Slot Coordinator;Aircraft Operator Representative;Network Operations Liaison;Meteorology Briefing Officer;Airport Duty Manager;Tower Supervisor(Brindle:section-only voice-drills);Ramp Control Lead(Quartzline:voice/chat);Ground Handling Dispatcher;Deicing Coordinator;Emergency Response Coordinator;System Support Engineer;Data Governance Steward;Airspace Sector Planner;Military Airspace Liaison. Centres→Flight Intent Message→Adapter(authentication/validation/Registry-mapping)→Exchange;rejections→reasons.Prediction→demand/imbalance flags.Capacity compares Airport Capacity Plan/Airport Acceptance Rate/Storm Cell Snapshot.Allocation→Calculated Takeoff Time/arrival-opportunity/Target Off Block Time→airlines(Adapter/Portal).Ground Delay Program:capacity-before-preferences;authority-validated safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation first;scheduled next;discretionary last;fairness requires delay-equity/proportional-access/no-systematic-disadvantage;excessive cross-operator delay needs visible/logged rule.Preferences advisory;unready flights resequence.Coordinator reviews/confirms publication;Copperfin authorizes Capacity Reduction State rules. Saffron uses delay slip for unrepresented crew-connectivity exemption;evaluate safety/network/passenger impacts,crew-legality,lower-impact alternatives.Slot Coordinator logs acceptance/rejection,rule,approver,consequence;Steward versions

New part:
S252: The Capacity Assessment Module applies the active Airport Capacity Plan and Airport Acceptance Rate to determine whether the proposed demand pattern remains operationally feasible.
S253: The Slot Allocation Engine derives the Calculated Takeoff Time by combining runway metering constraints, departure fix loading, and applicable Ground Delay Program rules.
S254: The Tower Sequence Manager maintains the tactical runway sequence expectation and highlights cases where the Calculated Takeoff Time is inconsistent with the local departure order.
S255: The Ramp Movement Board maintains milestone timestamps for stand readiness, boarding completion, doors closed, start approval readiness, taxi start, and other locally configured departure events.
S256: The Time Synchronization Service provides the reference clock for all target time calculations so that negotiation records and operational timestamps can be compared without local clock ambiguity.
S257: For voice coordination, Halcyon is the operational call sign used by the Slot Coordinator during daily target time conferences.
S258: The Slot Coordinator reviews proposed Calculated Takeoff Time values against network constraints and requests adjustment when the allocation would create avoidable delay or unfair sequencing.
S259: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews the proposed Target Off Block Time against aircraft readiness, crew availability, passenger connection risk, and operator recovery priorities.
S260: Saffron shall confirm any operator-requested Target Off Block Time revision in the Airport CDM Portal before the freeze horizon expires.
S261: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates handling milestones when service completion forecasts change, and those updates are treated as negotiation inputs until the freeze point is reached.
S262: The Ramp Control Lead assesses whether the proposed off-block pattern is compatible with apron access, stand conflicts, and local movement restrictions.
S263: The Tower Supervisor may challenge a proposed Calculated Takeoff Time when runway configuration, wake spacing, or local sequencing conditions make the value operationally unsuitable.
S264: The Airport CDM Portal presents each proposed value with its confidence status, last update time, and the reason code assigned by the proposing function or authorized user.
S265: The Common Situation Display shows the current agreed target set so that operational participants can see whether a flight is proposed, under negotiation, frozen, or exempted from compliance monitoring.
S266: Negotiation remains collaborative while the value is outside the freeze horizon, and each accepted amendment replaces the prior value as the current shared plan.
S267: The Collaborative Decision Log records each challenge, counterproposal, acceptance, rejection, and reason code associated with the Target Off Block Time and Calculated Takeoff Time.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
